title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
read_level: full (arXiv HTML v1; short paper, Secs 1-6 and Table 1; Figure 1 not viewed)
why_wsp: Benchmark in which LLM agents read, fix, write, compress weights or refuse infeasible edits of subject networks (2K-param MLPs to 7B LMs) inside an audited sandbox that meters forward passes.
domain: General WSP benchmark: control policies, games (Breakout, Go), small/7B language models, compression
editor: Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, DeepSeek v4-flash, GPT-6.1-sol (Claude Fable 5.1 ongoing, not reported)
target: 42 tasks; subject networks from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models
interface: code/tensor tools (sandboxed agent with metered NumPy and Weight API; Claude Code / Codex CLI scaffolds)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (agentic, with budgeted metered probes/forward passes per task; READ tasks N_forward=0)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: null (edit cost is a scored component: 'the smaller of the L_0 parameter count fraction and the matrix rank fraction'; no per-run counts reported)

headline_results.quote: Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215)
on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546
Opus reached 0.829 when synthesizing weights zero-shot from scratch, against Sonnet ( 0.569 ), Haiku ( 0.369 ) and DeepSeek ( 0.000 ); GPT-6.1-sol reached 0.863
the three Claude models performed alike, between 0.485 and 0.500 on every task, which is essentially the baseline of random guessing
All agents performed poorly on TR-05 (Hardware-Aware Optimization), between 0.177 and 0.238
On the four reasoning-loop tasks, only Opus (on three) and Sonnet (on one) scored above zero.
Currently 39 out of the 42 tasks clear this validity gate at their default difficulty levels.

cost.claim: GPU time for loop tasks (reason GPT-6.1-sol skipped them)
cost.quote: the four TR-02 reasoning-loop tasks, each of which needs one to one and a half GPU-hours per run

baselines_and_controls: Non-agentic baselines and static reference solutions per track (21 of 42 references use only agent-accessible info; others privileged, e.g. gradient fitting); validity gate: reference S_WB>=0.5 and >=0.2 over baseline.
runs_and_variance: Single seed (seed 0), default difficulty; two samples per task for Claude models, one for DeepSeek and GPT-6.1-sol; no variance reported. Quote: 'All runs evaluate the default difficulty level on a fixed seed (seed 0), with two samples per task for the Claude models and one for DeepSeek and GPT-6.1-sol'
robustness_of_edits: collateral damage on held-out benchmarks (e.g. MMLU) is a scored component; no fine-tuning/quantization survival tests
verification: Hash-chained ledger of metered forward passes/probes; operator-level tracing via metered NumPy subclass to detect forward-pass chains; automated audit with 28 quarantine flags. Quote: 'The final scores are computed directly from this ledger rather than the agent's outputs.'
memorization_vs_reasoning: Contamination mitigation via regenerated subject models with fresh seeds, rotations and hidden-dimension permutations 'so that the agents must analyze the weights rather than memorize indices'; no ablation reported measuring its effect.
limitations_stated: No dedicated limitations section. Stated: quarantined runs unreviewed so 'all scores are lower bounds'; GPT-6.1-sol not run on 4 loop tasks and 10 of its runs used a different scaffold; Claude Fable 5.1 evaluation incomplete; 3 tasks fail validity gate.
cites_or_builds_on: Han et al. 2026 weight-space learning survey
notes_for_survey: First benchmark in this corpus spanning READ/FIX/META/WRITE/SYSTEMS tracks with a composite score penalizing collateral damage, edit size and compute. Single seed, 1-2 samples per task, mixed scaffolds; results reported as lower bounds due to unreviewed quarantines.
